items.title: Machine Learning Beyond Statistical Consistency for Hybrid AI
items.summary: Machine learning is redefined as successfully computing a function with a proper derivation in a formal system, extending Gödel's theorem to empirical targets. Learning true probability requires both a Truth Condition (convergence to the true probability) and an Assurance Condition (the machine deriving its own convergence). Learning therefore extends beyond statistical consistency to necessitate a derivation of convergence from the observed record. Modern AI is hybrid, combining probabilistic tasks like prediction with deductive tasks like proving and coding. This framework explains the hybrid nature of modern AI within a single formal system.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Machine Learning Beyond Statistical Consistency for Hybrid AI" details a redefinition of machine learning by extending Gödel's theorem to empirical targets, establishing that learning true probability requires both a Truth Condition and an Assurance Condition. The research posits that learning extends beyond statistical consistency to necessitate a derivation of convergence from the observed record, suggesting that modern artificial intelligence is inherently hybrid, combining probabilistic prediction with deductive tasks like proving and coding within a single formal system. This framework explains the hybrid nature of contemporary AI by integrating probabilistic and deductive processes. This development indicates a new formal system for understanding the hybrid nature of advanced artificial intelligence.

items.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
items.summary: The research proposes an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion for high-dimensional off-policy evaluation without sample splitting. This method estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk using only its training observations. It enables early stopping during gradient-descent without requiring data sample splitting. The criterion is shown to provide uniform consistency and near-oracle guarantees for neural networks under specific conditions. Experiments indicate that this correction reduces risk estimation error and improves reward model selection compared to held-out baselines.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction" reports a method for high-dimensional off-policy evaluation that utilizes an Onsager correction to estimate the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk from training observations. The research proposes an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates risk using only the training data, enabling early stopping during gradient-descent without sample splitting. The methodology demonstrates that this criterion provides uniform consistency and near-oracle guarantees for neural networks under specified conditions. Experiments showed that this correction reduces risk estimation error and improves reward model selection when compared to standard held-out baselines. This advancement facilitates more robust and data-efficient policy evaluation in complex machine learning scenarios.

items.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
items.summary: The research explores kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, emphasizing how regularity affects kernel selection. It establishes embeddings of analytic operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The study provides finite-sample, high-probability guarantees for uncertainty based on sampling, showing exponential rates for analytic kernels and polynomial rates for Sobolev-type kernels. The theory is applied to the solution operator of parametric elliptic PDEs, separating sampling and discretization errors. Ultimately, the work prescribes how mesh size should relate to sample size for accurate approximations.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs" explores kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples and establishes embeddings of these operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The research provides finite-sample, high-probability guarantees for uncertainty based on sampling, demonstrating exponential rates for analytic kernels and polynomial rates for Sobolev-type kernels. The methodology is applied to the solution operator of parametric elliptic partial differential equations, successfully separating sampling and discretization errors. The study ultimately prescribes the relationship between mesh size and sample size necessary for accurate approximations. This work offers new theoretical frameworks for uncertainty quantification in operator learning and numerical analysis. Future developments are expected in applying these principles to complex systems modeling.

items.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
items.summary: Score-Repellent Monte Carlo improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density using the score function. Geometry-Aware SRMC generalizes this by incorporating a symmetric positive-definite matrix $M$ for anisotropic landscapes. The method identifies the optimal direction by relating the Fisher information to the repulsion-side matrix. This approach yields a bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, providing theoretical guarantees for online implementation. Experimental results show GA-SRMC significantly outperforms SRMC in terms of ESS for various targets.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo" describes a method that improves Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling by tilting the target density using the score function, with the key finding being the introduction of a geometry-aware approach for anisotropic landscapes. The methodology involves incorporating a symmetric positive-definite matrix M into the Score-Repellent Monte Carlo framework to account for the landscape geometry. The method identifies the optimal direction by relating the Fisher information to the repulsion-side matrix, resulting in a bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix that provides theoretical guarantees for online implementation. Experimental results indicate that Geometry-Aware SRMC demonstrates a significant improvement in effective sample size compared to standard SRMC across various target distributions. This advancement suggests a new direction for developing more efficient sampling techniques in complex statistical modeling.

items.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
items.summary: The lower-star filtration (LSF) is limited because it can fill topological features immediately, resulting in incomplete persistence diagrams. Three alternative filtration methods are proposed to address this limitation: $\varepsilon$-lower-star filtration (ELSF), $L_p$ filtration ($L_p F$), and softmax filtration (SMF). These alternatives introduce dimension-dependent delays or use aggregation functions based on all vertex values instead of just the maximum. These modifications allow topological features to persist over longer intervals, potentially revealing more information about data structures. Experimental results show that these methods are computationally efficient and offer greater sensitivity to data differences than LSF.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology" details three alternative methods for persistent homology filtration. These methods address limitations in the lower-star filtration by introducing dimension-dependent delays or using aggregation functions based on all vertex values instead of just the maximum, allowing topological features to persist over longer intervals. The proposed alternatives include the epsilon-lower-star filtration, L_p filtration, and softmax filtration. Experimental results indicate that these modifications are computationally efficient and demonstrate greater sensitivity to data differences compared to the lower-star filtration. This research suggests new approaches for analyzing data structures where topological features are relevant. The development points toward improved methods for feature extraction in machine learning applications.

items.title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation
items.summary: Language model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly, with earlier choices affecting later contexts. The study analyzes selection among candidates by comparing cumulative loss against the best initial configuration. Excess loss is broken down into regret within the family, the gap from the family, and the impact of the deployment history. Sublinear expected regret is achieved when switching limits the scope, and fewer switches can either improve or worsen deployed loss. Experiments suggest that text-only selection has lower regret but more failures than joint selection.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation" analyzes the selection process in language model adaptation and presents findings on regret. The study investigated how language model systems repeatedly select prompts and parameter adapters, determining the impact of earlier choices on subsequent contexts. Researchers compared cumulative loss against the best initial configuration to quantify the excess loss, breaking it down into regret within the family, the gap from the family, and the influence of deployment history. Sublinear expected regret was achieved when switching limits the scope, and fewer switches demonstrated the potential to either improve or worsen deployed loss. Text-only selection demonstrated lower regret but resulted in more failures than joint selection approaches. This research provides a framework for optimizing adaptation strategies within language model deployment.

items.title: ELPAC: Endpoint-Anchored Latent Progression with Stage-Varying Multimodal Coordination
items.summary: ELPAC is a Bayesian framework designed to jointly infer latent aging stages and progression subtypes from multimodal data. It integrates subtype trajectories by working backward from endpoint groups using biologically structured velocity components. The method further factorizes residual multimodal variation into sparse coordination axes that reveal subtype-specific patterns. ELPAC employs a scalable variational inference scheme for joint posterior inference at the cohort level. Testing on Alzheimer's data shows ELPAC accurately recovers latent structures and provides biologically interpretable multimodal coordination programs.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "ELPAC: Endpoint-Anchored Latent Progression with Stage-Varying Multimodal Coordination" reports on a Bayesian framework designed to jointly infer latent aging stages and progression subtypes from multimodal data, achieving accurate recovery of latent structures and biologically interpretable multimodal coordination programs in Alzheimer's data. The ELPAC method integrates subtype trajectories by working backward from endpoint groups utilizing biologically structured velocity components. The approach further factorizes residual multimodal variation into sparse coordination axes that reveal subtype-specific patterns. A scalable variational inference scheme is employed for joint posterior inference at the cohort level, demonstrating the capacity to uncover latent aging structures. This work provides a method for interpreting complex biological multimodal data through latent variable modeling. The development suggests new avenues for applying advanced probabilistic methods to model complex biological progression.

items.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
items.summary: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles introduces BRINE, a data-driven method to equalize noise variance across rows and columns in noisy matrices. This procedure aims to resolve the distortion caused by heteroskedasticity, which obscures weak signals in large datasets. The core technique involves equating the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing unknown noise variances. The method restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal structure. The approach proves convergence to the true equalizer with geometric rates, providing estimates directly from noisy data.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles" introduces BRINE, a data-driven method to equalize noise variance across rows and columns in noisy matrices. The method addresses the distortion caused by heteroskedasticity in large datasets by equating the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing unknown noise variances. The core technique involves this procedure to resolve the distortion obscuring weak signals, and it restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum. This approach allows for the amplification of signal components without any prior knowledge of the signal structure, demonstrating convergence to the true equalizer with geometric rates directly estimated from the noisy data. This development offers a new technique for processing large noisy matrices in data analysis applications.

items.title: Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport
items.summary: The method introduces structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics to assess if empirical time-series dynamics align with a prescribed predictable-drift class. It translates stochastic path properties into a finite-dimensional projection problem over empirical transition laws, using row-wise moment constraints for admissibility. Deviations are quantified by a Kullback-Leibler projection gap, $G_{\lambda,k}$. This yields a diagnostic and a scalable Bregman-Dykstra algorithm that incorporates structural constraints into Sinkhorn-type methods. The technique can distinguish between process classes that share identical second-order statistics, acting as a general tool for sequential data model validation.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport" introduces structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics to assess if empirical time-series dynamics align with a prescribed predictable-drift class. The method translates stochastic path properties into a finite-dimensional projection problem over empirical transition laws, utilizing row-wise moment constraints for admissibility. Deviations between the empirical dynamics and the prescribed drift class are quantified by a Kullback-Leibler projection gap, denoted as G lambda k. This process yields both a diagnostic and a scalable Bregman-Dykstra algorithm that incorporates structural constraints into Sinkhorn-type methods. The technique demonstrates the ability to distinguish between process classes that possess identical second-order statistics, offering a general tool for sequential data model validation. This work provides a rigorous method for validating the structural consistency of time-series data models. Further research will explore the application of this framework to complex generative models.

items.title: pESTO: Iterative p-greedy kernel regression with risk-driven Early STOpping
items.summary: Kernel-based greedy algorithms, often p-greedy, select approximation nodes by minimizing point-wise error indicators. In noisy data, the separation of approximation error and noise amplification is crucial, which is governed by the power function and a Lebesgue-type term. This motivates using the Stein's unbiased risk estimator (SURE) as a proxy for the mean squared error. SURE provides a principled stopping criterion for selecting the number of nodes in the p-greedy procedure. Numerical experiments confirm that this method effectively balances deterministic accuracy and statistical noise.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "pESTO: Iterative p-greedy kernel regression with risk-driven Early STOpping" details a method for kernel-based greedy algorithms incorporating risk-driven stopping criteria. Kernel-based greedy algorithms, frequently p-greedy, select approximation nodes by minimizing point-wise error indicators. The separation of approximation error from noise amplification is addressed using a power function and a Lebesgue-type term in noisy data, leading to the motivation for using Stein's unbiased risk estimator as a proxy for the mean squared error. This approach provides a principled stopping criterion for the p-greedy procedure by utilizing SURE. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this method effectively balances deterministic accuracy and statistical noise in the regression process. This development offers a means to improve the efficiency and reliability of kernel regression techniques in complex datasets.
